title: What Is Taken to Have Already Been Made Available on the Card
content:
Where an allowance still owed is reckoned on a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card, what has already been made available is read from the card's own load entries, net of anything taken back from them.

What has already been made available is the total of the loads posted on the card, where the card carries at least one load and nothing has been taken back from it; it is the loads posted less what has been taken back, where the card carries a load and an allowance taken back for want of spending; and it is nothing in every other case.

**Which entries are counted.** The loads posted are the scheduled load entries and the extra load entries on the card's running record, taken together. What has been taken back is the total of the entries ending a benefit period's allowance that was not used. The count that decides which row applies is the count of the scheduled load entries.

| The card's record | What has already been made available |
|---|---|
| at least one load, and nothing taken back for want of spending | the total of the loads posted |
| at least one load, and an allowance taken back for want of spending | the loads posted less what has been taken back |
| no load at all | nothing |

**Worked through on hypothetical entries.** A card carrying scheduled loads of 90.00 USD and 90.00 USD and no allowance taken back: what has already been made available is 180.00 USD. The same card carrying an allowance taken back of 46.80 USD: 133.20 USD. A card carrying no load entry at all: nothing.
